sources.entry: Audioserve - Simple personal server to serve audio files from directories (audiobooks, music, podcasts...). Focused on simplicity and supports sync of play position between clients. MIT Rust

summary.one_liner: Audioserve is a simple, minimalist Rust server for streaming personal audio collections (audiobooks, music, podcasts) from ordinary directories, with play position sync across clients.
summary.what_it_does: Serves audio files directly from folder structures on disk, using the directory layout for browsing and search (folder names only). It caches collection metadata in an embedded sled database so search and folder loading are fast, and watches directories for changes (inotify on Linux) so edits show up automatically. It supports single-file audiobooks such as .m4b by presenting chapters as virtual files, and can collapse CD subfolders into one folder. On-the-fly transcoding to Opus, MP3 or AAC through ffmpeg is offered in low, medium and high quality levels. Playback positions are shared between devices in the same group over WebSocket, with optional JSON backup. The README also describes a PWA web client, an older Android client, and a documented API.
use_cases: stream audiobooks from a home server
serve a personal music or podcast library over the web
sync listening position between phone and desktop
transcode audio to low-bitrate Opus for slow connections
host an audiobook collection for a small trusted group
play chaptered .m4b files chapter by chapter
notable: Browses by real directory structure rather than audio tags, which the author argues are unreliable
Collections cache in embedded key-value database, with inotify-based change watching
Alternative transcoding profiles selected by User-Agent, e.g. AAC for Apple devices
Playback position sharing via WebSocket with JSON backup and restore
Optional HTTP/2, TLS, CORS, rate limiting and reverse-proxy support
caveats: Transcoding needs ffmpeg on PATH and is CPU-heavy; the README advises only a few parallel transcodes per core
Apple platforms need extra configuration for the default Opus/Ogg transcoding; AAC alternative is required
Android client is no longer maintained; the web client is recommended instead
Intended for moderate personal collections, not large multi-user deployments
keywords: 媒体 server alternative to subsonic
